items.caption: How much it cost to clean this home for free! @outreachtalentgroup #cleaning #money #beforeandafter #hometransformations
items.transcript: I had six days to stop an elderly woman from losing her home and I'm gonna tell you exactly how much it cost me. The living room was hoarded from floor to ceiling, there was an active mice infestation, most of the lights didn't work and I had six days to clean the entire home otherwise the elderly woman living here would be evicted. Now normally a home this size would have taken Harry and I almost two weeks but with a six-day deadline we called in reinforcements. I told my management at OTG about my dilemma and lucky for me Dylan, Jodie, Jess, Rebecca, Rhys and Niamh all were willing to take a day off work and come and help and trust me we needed them. Our first big expense was £1,408 on waste removal. It probably should have been double that price but the clearance company I use are angels. Now despite how this home looked, the resident is not a hoarder. After losing someone she loved and going through a severe depressive episode that lasted years, her home became completely overwhelming. She was ready to let almost everything go and start again, she just couldn't do it alone and she simply couldn't afford the help she needed. So her family contacted me because I clean for free and I only clean for people in need. Next we spent £730 on PPE to keep our lovely volunteers safe and another £475 on transport. Now normally a big chunk of the cost also comes from accommodation both for me and for the resident of the free clean. But I stayed at a friend's house nearby and the resident's family offered to pay for her to stay in a hotel during the clean so that was also free for me. The cost of cleaning supplies was almost free too because I already had most of what we needed although I did have to spend £80 replacing things we ran out of mid-clean. And when we finally finished emptying and cleaning the home we spent £1,885 refurnishing it. Which means the total cost of this clean was £4,578. But let me tell you it should have been a lot more. The truth is I can't put a price on an entire team giving up their time to help a stranger to keep her home. I also can't put a price on her family helping her to repaint and replace the flooring or the council workers and social care teams who worked tirelessly to make sure all repairs were completed and the mice infestation was dealt with after we left. And then there's you. Every time you watch one of these videos that money goes towards the next free clean. Make no mistake bestie I may be the person that's cleaning on screen but thousands of people have helped make this happen. Because of everyone who watches my videos six days later the elderly resident got to keep her home. This is what it looked like after the clean was complete. Now obviously it's not perfect but once the walls are repainted and the floors are replaced it will be good as new.

items.caption: Emergency bathroom clean to save elderly woman from eviction #cleaning #beforeandafter #homemakeover #eviction #bathroomcleaning
items.transcript: This is an emergency free deep clean to save an elderly woman from eviction. The toilet doesn't flush, the shower barely works, and the bathtub is full of mice. Despite her children now being fully grown, the contents of this bathroom suggested that their mother had been holding on to traces of their childhood for all these years. And based off the scale of the hoard in here, I'm guessing this bathroom hasn't been functional for a long time. So let's clean it for free! Now when I posted my last video, a lot of you assumed the council were evicting her because of the condition of the flat. No, no baby, that's not how it works in the UK. We have renters rights. What actually happened is the council had been trying to carry out mandatory safety checks for years, but the resident wouldn't let them in. Without those checks, they couldn't legally deem the property safe to live in, leaving them no choice but to evict her. And speaking of eviction, loads of you guys were asking what I did about the mice infestation. The answer is nothing. I don't want to kill or harm any animal and I'm also not going to be laying down traps or poison bait either. My job was to remove the rubbish, food and all the hiding places that were allowing the infestation to thrive in the first place. Now you might not agree with that boundary, but it's my boundary, so argue with your mama. Now on my last video, I got a little bit of criticism. People were rightfully concerned about me introducing new furnishings while there was still an active mice infestation. But in full transparency, we only did that a few hours before the council arrived to carry out their checks, start the repairs and deal with the infestation. So although refurnishing at this point wasn't ideal, the alternative was leaving an elderly woman with no bed, no proper shower and an empty shell of a home. I don't know about you, but I would much rather give her something comfortable to come home to. I want her to be able to have a shower, use a nice hair mask and feel clean and pampered afterwards. I want her to be able to go to the toilet and sit on a new toilet seat instead of having to squat over a broken one. And I want her at the end of the day to be able to get into a nice clean bed with a new mattress and fresh bedding and have her first restful night's sleep in years. Little things like this restore so much dignity for someone who's been struggling for so long. And don't get me wrong, a face cream and a free clean is not going to rewrite years of trauma and mental illness. But it does help to remind the resident that they are worthy of help and they are worthy of a better life. So that's what we did and I'm so glad we made that decision. That's the before and afters. If you want to see the rest of the clean, drop me a follow and I'll catch you in the next one.

items.caption: Emergency Free Clean to Avoid Eviction! #cleaning #beforeandafter #homemakeover #eviction
items.transcript: I have six days to deep clean this entire flat. And if I don't, the elderly woman who lives here will be evicted and lose her home. Her entire flat has become hoarded and infested with mice. They've chewed through almost everything, including the mattress that she'd been sleeping on. Her kitchen was no longer usable, so she created this makeshift one instead in the corner of the bedroom. And if anyone was wondering, no, her family had absolutely no idea she was living like this. Like many people struggling with their mental health, this resident had become very good at hiding just how bad things had gotten. By the time her family found out, the council had already issued an eviction notice. And that's when they contacted me, which means that this has very quickly become an emergency free clean. And I'm not just cleaning this bedroom, I have to do the entire flat. So I'm going to stop yapping and start cleaning. Because we're going to have to speed run a few things. The carpet needs ripping out, the walls need repainting, and obviously the mouse infestation needs to be dealt with. But there is some really good news. If I can get this property cleaned, cleared, and safe enough for the council to properly access it, they've said that they're willing to help with the repairs and the infestation. Meaning the elderly woman who lives here will be able to move back in and keep her home. So the pressure is on. We have six days, and judging by this bedroom alone, we're going to need every single minute of them. And if you're still watching, this butt shakes for you. Every time you watch and interact with my videos, you are directly funding the next free clean for someone who needs it. Because of you, for the first time in years, this elderly resident now has a bed. And yes, we still need to get flooring and all of the walls repainted, and we need to deal with the mice infestation. But like I said before, that is being done. If you want to see the rest of this home transformation, drop me a follow, and I'll see you in the next one. I love ya!

items.caption: The final before & after of this free clean home transformation and how much it cost me to complete ❤️ #cleaning #beforeandafter #transformation #money
items.transcript: This bed was the cleanest part of this entire home. It was stained with blood, soaked in urine, and it can't have been safe or pleasant for the resident to sleep in every night. So like everything else contaminated in this home, it's gotta go. Now I always get asked how much these free cleans cost me, so let's break this one down together. But first, I need to state the obvious. I only clean for people in need and I only clean for free. The residents never pay a penny, but that doesn't mean the clean doesn't cost anything. Now full transparency, this was one of the cheapest free cleans I've ever done. Sadly, this home was contaminated with human waste, blood, and used needles, so almost everything had to be sent for specialist biohazard incineration. That alone cost £1,054. Additionally, the police had previously forced the front door open during a welfare check, so before we could even get inside the property and think of starting to clean, I had to pay a locksmith £150 to make the property secure again. Because the clean was so far from home, travel cost me £267 and my Airbnb for the week came to £464. The resident couldn't stay in the property while we cleaned because it simply wasn't safe. She had nowhere else to go, so I paid £459 for her Airbnb plus a £150 deposit that I told her she could keep if she kept the Airbnb clean, which she did. Sadly, most of her clothes weren't salvageable, so I gave her a £100 gift card so she could replace some of her essentials. Cleaning products, respirators, hospital grade disinfectants and sanitizers came to £299. Then we spent another £399 at B&M replacing bedding, toiletries, rugs, storage and other essentials. Her new mattress cost £120, her replacement gaming chair was £80 and that brings the total cost of this free clean to £3,692. Now I know that's a lot of money, but surprisingly it's actually one of the cheapest free cleans I've ever done. Normally they cost a lot more. And the reason I'm sharing this is because I want people to understand why so many that are living in unsafe homes like this one rarely get the help they desperately need. Most people simply can't afford it. And yeah, a professional cleaning company wouldn't be replacing furniture and personal belongings like I do, but they would rightfully be charging for the specialist training, equipment and labour needed to carry out a clean like this safely. Like most creators, I earn money when people watch and engage with my videos and that money is put right back into funding the next free clean. So every time you watch one of my videos or comment on it, you are directly funding the next free clean and you are directly helping someone to receive the help they otherwise wouldn't be able to afford. Because of you, this young woman now has a clean bed, a safe home and a chance to begin rebuilding her life.
